title: Integral finite reduction and derived tensor
statement: For every prime l, finite field extension E of Q_l, scheme X, index n and K in D(Mod(O_E,X)), the restriction to O_E,X of the actual derived extension to the continuous finite quotient at level n+1 is isomorphic to the derived tensor reductionFunctor at n+1.

proof.text: Choose a K-flat representative. The derived-extension counit is invertible there. Exact scalar restriction commutes with localization.

The balanced tensor universal property identifies restricted extension with tensoring by the restricted regular finite quotient. The mapMod-comap comparison and the strong monoidal unit isomorphism identify this quotient module with the pulled-back quotientModule.

The K-flat tensor model identifies the resulting localized complex with derived tensor by that degree-zero module. Compose with the representative isomorphism. This is an objectwise comparison, which suffices for vanishing. No boundedness or flatness of the quotient is used.

theorem derived_nakayama_reduction_comparison
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E] (X : Scheme.{u}) (n : ℕ)
    (K : DerivedCategory (AdicCompletion.Modules l E X)) :
    Nonempty (AdicCompletion.integralLevel l E X K n ≅
      (DerivedNakayama.reductionFunctor l E X (n + 1)).obj K)
